findings.source_en: Well, no sense in lettin’ it go to waste.
findings.ar: وعلى أي حال، من العبث أن ندعه يضيع، وقد مات أخوه في الحرب.
findings.issue: Arabic adds a fabricated clause 'and his brother died in the war' that has no basis anywhere in the English source line.
findings.suggested_ar: وعلى أي حال، من العبث أن ندعه يضيع.

findings.issue: Line is addressed to Proxima (female, named in the same sentence), but mixes masculine أنتَ with feminine ذي — should be fully feminine.
Glossary freezes 'Hexapod' as السداسيّ الأرجل; this row uses an unapproved transliteration instead.

findings.source_en: Every brigand within fifty miles has probably been here.
findings.ar: لا يمكنك الجزم بذلك؛ فلم ينتهِ البحث بعد.
findings.issue: This Arabic is actually the translation of the sibling row 90E99614417F71E54241C188B86BB8A0 ('You cannot know that. There is more to search.') — the two rows' Arabic content is swapped.
findings.suggested_ar: الأرجح أن كل لصٍّ في نطاق خمسين ميلًا مرّ من هنا.

findings.source_en: There’s not really much to tell.
findings.issue: English says there ISN'T much to tell; Arabic states the opposite — that there IS actually much to tell, frankly.

Scene context (Merrick chiding Proxima over the healing 'deal' she made, followed by her apology and his 'you still owe me') indicates the addressee is Proxima (female); verb uses masculine عقدتَ instead of feminine.

findings.source_en: But why? What did the, uh, Hexapod do to you?
findings.ar: لكن لماذا؟ ماذا فعل بك ذلك... الهكسابود؟
findings.issue: Same frozen-term violation as the standalone 'Hexapod.' row — glossary requires السداسيّ الأرجل, not the transliteration.
findings.suggested_ar: لكن لماذا؟ ماذا فعل بك ذلك... السداسيّ الأرجل؟

findings.issue: The Brigand King is mocking Proxima's claim ('My weapon. You have it.') — addressee is Proxima (female), but the diacritic explicitly marks masculine سلاحكَ instead of feminine.

findings.source_en: Can’t you just stick that… probe in me again?
findings.ar: ألا يمكنك أن تغرزي فيّ ذلك... المسبار مرة أخرى؟
findings.issue: Proxima (the injured speaker, 'I am severely injured') is asking Merrick (male) to use the probe on her again; the verb uses feminine تغرزي, addressing the wrong gender.
findings.suggested_ar: ألا يمكنك أن تغرز فيّ ذلك... المسبار مرة أخرى؟
